evidence:
Workbook 'Quality Checks' row 11 (B - task.toml & run wiring): 'Agent, verifier, liveness, and judge timeouts are long enough and nest: gate judges < gates budget, scored judges < scored budget, both budgets < verifier timeout.' Internal Quality Checks row 11: '...nest properly (inner < outer, sum of judges < verifier).' Deterministic sheet check-scoring-policy.py also checks that judge timeouts nest inside suite budgets and the verifier timeout. Skill references/quality-checks.md:50-51 ('do the arithmetic and show it ... [agent].timeout_sec is enough for the build; build_timeout_sec exceeds a realistic cold build'); staged-task-contract.md:111 (gates 1500, scored 11100, verifier 13200); NEW_TASK_AUTHORING_CONTEXT.md:112 (--max-concurrent-agent 1, compute serial totals).

ARITHMETIC (frozen task .qc-cache/hireops-lessons-2026-10-08-r4/task):
- task.toml:17-18 agent timeout_sec=7200.0; :21 build_timeout_sec=600.0; :27 verifier timeout_sec=13200.0. All equal to the frozen template task.toml values.
- tests/test.sh is byte-identical to the frozen template test.sh (diff clean): :213 run_suite gates 1500; :224 run_suite scored 11100; :207 rewardkit --max-concurrent-agent 1 (serial).
- Gates: render judge.toml:4 timeout=600 batched, constraints judge.toml:4 timeout=600 batched -> 600+600=1200 < 1500 (300 s slack). PASS.
- Scored: functional judge.toml:3-4 mode='individual', timeout=700 with 12 [[criterion]] blocks. RewardKit 0.1.7 individual mode runs each criterion sequentially as a fresh CLI call with the same judge.timeout (deliverables/colderwater-playground-devtools/structural-review-2026-09-27/harness/ARCHITECTURE_ASSESSMENT.md:19; codearena-task-breaker/references/verification.md:121-124 'judge timeout is per criterion'). Worst case 12x700=8400; polish batched 900 (5 criteria); visual batched 900 (5 likert) -> 8400+900+900=10200 < 11100 (900 s slack). PASS.
- Verifier: 1500+11100=12600 < 13200 (600 s slack for copy, app launch with ~30 s liveness loop test.sh:115-122, score.py twice). PASS.
- Liveness: test.sh:116-121 120 x 0.25 s probe (~30 s nominal); the restart helper's identical 30 s loop is nested inside restart_mcp.py HELPER_TIMEOUT_SEC=55 (tools/restart_mcp.py:11, identical to template). PASS.
- Agent 7200 s / build 600 s are template canonical; environment/Dockerfile is node:22-bookworm-slim + apt (4 small packages) + npm -g express@5.1.0 better-sqlite3@12.4.1, a realistic cold build well below 600 s (not measured in this round). Agent budget is ample for a hand-built Node/Express/SQLite app; not measured.

'LONG ENOUGH' - NOT MEASURED, CREDIBLE RISK:
- The template ships functional as batched timeout=9000; this task changed it to individual/700 (functional judge.toml:3-4). The comment at :23 explains the mode and weights only; no recorded workload reason, measurement or authorization for the 700 s per-criterion value was found (grep of handoffs/, projects/hireops-recruiting-operations, qc/*.md, root *.md). Suite budgets are unchanged, so the nest holds, but each functional session now has a hard 700 s ceiling.
- Every functional session must first repeat the minimal backend check (functional/prompt.md:15: sign in, add a candidate, reload, open an independent context via browser_run_code_unsafe, sign in as Observer, find the card) before its own steps, and must report every step (:31-33). Heavy criteria: hro_moves (weight 7, 2282 chars) prescribes creating a job, adding 5 candidates, ~25 moves/rejections/undos/reopens with refusal attempts and two independent-context Mei Lin reads; hro_intake_restart (4.5) opens 2 jobs plus 5 refused job attempts incl. a request replay, adds 6 candidates plus 3 email attempts, an independent read, a note, a message, restart_app (up to 55 s) and a full fresh-context comparison; hro_undo_activity (7, 2561 chars); hro_unread_seen/hro_messaging/hro_two_people include 15 s timed observations (+2 s settle, up to 3 attempts each, prompt.md:29). With claude-code + z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx driving Playwright MCP, these are plausibly 60-100+ tool turns; at several seconds per turn that is on the order of the 700 s ceiling. This is an estimate, not a measurement.
- Consequence if exceeded: RewardKit returns an error row scored 0 for that criterion and still exits 0 (ARCHITECTURE_ASSESSMENT.md:27, local probe), and tools/score.py:40-48 consumes the dimension score without any error/incomplete check, so a correct app would silently lose e.g. 7/61 of functional (about 0.069 reward) - a harness failure attributed to the submission. prompt.md:35 makes the judge return 'NOT EXERCISED' binary 0 when the budget is exhausted, which is still scored 0.
- Polish: 5 multi-context live/timed criteria in one 900 s batched session (several 15 s watches with repeats, session resume) - also unmeasured.
- Raw evidence index (all 8 artifact hashes re-verified as matching) states 'Full configured grading/workload ... absent', and each entry is 'Not a configured judge run, Oracle grade, model score or judge-duration measurement.' The scripted golden run (workspace.json, 26 groups PASS, via-solve.log) is not judge duration (REVIEW_POLICY.md:25; lessons #19).

LESSONS_FROM_COLDERWATER checks bearing on row 11: #7/#14 timing steps run in one code-runner action with up to two repeats - present in functional prompt.md:29, but each attempt consumes time inside the 700 s per-criterion ceiling; #11 judge infra timeouts zero a criterion/dimension - applies directly and score.py does not detect it; #17-#19 a scripted golden harness is not configured judge timing - no full configured run exists for this candidate; #10 prompt size belongs to another row (largest assembled functional prompt is ~8.6 KB prompt + 1.9 KB context + one criterion, far below 128 KB). No timeout was increased; no shared harness file (test.sh, restart_mcp.py) differs from the template.

Alternatives: a conforming but slower-to-drive app (e.g. confirmation dialogs on every move, a paged board) raises hro_moves tool turns and is the most likely to hit 700 s while being fully correct; a broken app that fails early finishes quickly and gains nothing. The budget can therefore only push a correct app downward, not lift a weak one.

Verdict rationale: the nesting arithmetic passes; the 'long enough' half rests on an unmeasured, unrecorded 700 s per-criterion ceiling for long multi-context criteria. Per the skill ('Never upgrade an unmeasured claim to Pass') and REVIEW_POLICY.md:25 ('Workload is measured, not inferred from a timeout number') this cannot be Pass; it is not demonstrated as a Fail either. Required runtime evidence is missing -> risk=true.
counterexample: Golden (correct) app under the configured judge: the hro_moves session (weight 7 of 61) must redo the minimal backend check, create a job, add 5 candidates, perform ~25 moves/rejections/undos/reopens with refusal attempts and two independent-context reads, then report every step; if this takes more than 700 s, RewardKit kills it, records an error row scored 0 and exits 0, and score.py (no error check) yields functional <= 54/61 for a fully correct app. Not measured either way.
suggested_fix: Run the full configured judge on the golden (and a target-builder app) and record per-criterion durations; if any functional session approaches 700 s, trim or split its steps (changing scope and coverage together), or raise the per-criterion timeout with a recorded reason and authorization while keeping 12 x timeout + 900 + 900 < 11100.
